title: ModMenu
summary: Game library, exact module drafts and legacy profile configuration over explicit host ports.

blocks.text: ui.mod-menu@1.0.0 creates a reusable browser/offline library view. Initialization needs no other capability. Each instance requires explicit DOM roles and a ModMenuLibraryPort; its host owns verified packages, persistence, code approval, exact profiles, world publication and download encoding. Shared floating chrome can host these roles without becoming a library database.

entries() returns display metadata only: opaque item ID, purpose, collection/favorite, explicit built-in status and code/data counts. Search, sorting and card rendering never receive archive blobs or live worlds. The current app adapter still opens/decodes its existing store; indexed metadata/lazy inspection optimization remains separate measured work.

The same owner creates modules(root, port, options) for exact v2 releases/capability/provider/settings drafts and profile(elements, port, initial) for intentional v1 compatibility. Host compatible() supplies metadata suggestions; this UI contains no second dependency resolver. A module dependency, capability contract and singleton provider choice stay distinct. Numeric help/defaults/bounds/steps are displayed without changing schemas or activating a draft.

The legacy profile editor exposes draft() and select() over public v1 manifests; it does not manufacture a v2 lock. Installed attribution, export/removal and compatible presentation settings route through explicit host commands. Active artifacts remain protected from removal. The host revalidates commands and exact candidate state before publication. Importing inert bytes, editing a draft and enabling a game are separate actions.

The release menu separates built-in controls, installed packages and bundled source packages. mountBundledCatalogue(root, entries) is an inert searchable source inventory: it never installs packages, changes a profile or proves runtime portability. The build generates its compact metadata from owned module descriptors and guide summaries. Legacy profile drafts survive unrelated menu refreshes and reset when the applied profile changes. Hosts create a fresh profile view when switching worlds or games, so unapplied edits do not leak between selections with identical profiles.

Import, save, export, play, organize and remove are explicit async host commands with an AbortSignal. Import must verify/install inert bytes and never implicitly activate code. Play must validate and stage a compatible candidate before publication. The host must check cancellation before changing the active world; committed inert storage writes need not be rolled back by view disposal. Organizing metadata must not silently change exact enabled package pins.

One command runs at a time. Rebuilding cards aborts their event handlers; removing a view aborts its pending command and restores borrowed list/status/disabled state. A late result cannot update the removed UI. The provider owns views and styles and rejects creation after disposal. Preserve minimal import/dependency recovery if this optional view is absent.

Current extraction preserves the existing game-library collection label and favorite UI. It does not implement hierarchical module folders, a collection archive format, workers, a marketplace, version upgrades or offline application generation. Portable game packs and ready-to-play offline applications are distinct. Public creator guidance and examples remain in the offline Creators Manual.
